newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: FMLN appears to take lead in key El Salvador votes.
newsitem.headline: FMLN appears to take lead in key El Salvador votes.

text.p: The left-wing Farabundo Marti Liberation Movement (FMLN) appeared to have scored important victories on Sunday in nationwide elections for El Salvador's Congress and for the job of mayor in the capital.
Although official results were still not known late on Sunday, the FMLN claimed victory, and the ruling right-wing National Republican Alliance (ARENA) appeared ready to acknowledge defeat.
The vote was a slap in the face for El Salvador President Armando Calderon Sol, a member of the ARENA party.
The Supreme Electoral Tribunal (TSE) said it was satisfied with the way the vote took place but had not yet released official results.
"I see that the Salvadorian people, apparently all the way to the national level, have decided to try an adventure," said Mario Valiente, ARENA director and current mayor of the capital San Salvador.
"I think that the adventure will be dangerous, but if it is the will of the people we are going to respect it," Valiente told a news conference.
He also recognised the victory of his rival for the post of mayor of the capital, doctor Hector Silva, who led a coalition headed by the FMLN.
"I am ready to govern," Silva, 49, told reporters.
FMLN campaign chief, Facundo Guardado, also claimed victory for his party in the fight for mayor of San Salvador and for other important cities in the country.
He also said the FMLN had 38 seats in Congress against 36 for the ARENA.
Turnout appeared to be poor but voting appeared to take place in an atmosphere of calm under the watchful eye of about 10,000 police and 1,000 international observers.
About 2.6 million voters had been eligible to choose from among 13 parties to fill positions for 84 deputies in Congress and for 262 mayors.
The FMLN, which transformed itself from a guerrilla movement into a democratic party, had hoped to make gains on the 20 seats it held in Congress, compared with ARENA's 39 seats before Sunday's vote.
During the 12-year civil war that ended with a stalemate and a peace treaty in January 1992, about 75,000 people lost their lives.
